content.value_statement: Multi-agent workflows often waste time, tokens, and compute through poor coordination. This skill guides profiling, workload distribution, cost controls, and measured optimization.
actual_capabilities: Defines baseline metrics and target performance goals before optimization.
Profiles database, application, and frontend agent workloads for bottlenecks.
Recommends context compression, relevance filtering, and token budget controls.
Designs parallel execution and dynamic workload distribution strategies.
Tracks token usage and supports cost-aware model selection.
Guides gradual rollouts with repeatable tests and rollback planning.
limitations: Provides guidance and illustrative pseudocode, not a complete executable framework.
Requires baseline metrics and evaluation data for meaningful recommendations.
Does not focus on tuning a single agent prompt.
Requires environment-specific testing before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Reduce Workflow Latency
use_cases.description: Profile agent handoffs, identify blocking work, and design parallel execution with measurable latency targets.

use_cases.title: Control LLM Costs
use_cases.description: Track token use, select models by task complexity, and define budget-aware context policies.
use_cases.target_user: Engineering managers responsible for AI spending

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Reliability
use_cases.description: Plan incremental orchestration changes, regression tests, quality thresholds, and rollback criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Establish a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-agent workflow: [workflow]. Identify measurable latency, throughput, quality, and cost baselines before proposing changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when beginning an optimization effort without a documented baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Profile Coordination Bottlenecks
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile [system] against [performance goals]. Map each agent's workload, dependencies, communication overhead, context use, and likely bottlenecks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when metrics exist but the source of poor performance is unclear.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incremental orchestration plan for [system] under [budget constraints]. Include workload distribution, parallelism, context controls, rollback steps, and evaluation metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when converting profiling evidence into controlled implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Competing Strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two orchestration strategies for [system] using [evaluation data]. Quantify cost, latency, throughput, reliability, and quality tradeoffs, then recommend a staged rollout.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when selecting a production strategy under several constraints.

output_examples.input: Analyze a sequential research workflow with four specialized agents and high response latency.
output: Baseline: Measure median and tail latency, throughput, token use, error rate, and task quality before changing orchestration.
Primary hypothesis: Sequential handoffs create idle time and repeated context transfer.
Next test: Parallelize independent research tasks, preserve deterministic aggregation, and compare results against the baseline.

output_examples.input: Reduce monthly model spending while maintaining answer quality.
output: Segment tasks by complexity and record quality, latency, and token cost for each segment.
Route routine work to lower-cost models and reserve stronger models for complex synthesis.
Set quality thresholds, budget alerts, caching rules, and a rollback condition before rollout.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe rollout for a new parallel agent orchestrator.
output: Start with replay tests against representative workflows and compare every target metric.
Release to a small traffic segment while monitoring errors, latency, cost, and output quality.
Expand gradually only when thresholds hold, with the previous orchestrator available for rollback.

best_practices: Measure performance, quality, and cost before and after every optimization.
Change one orchestration variable at a time when practical.
Use staged rollouts, explicit thresholds, and tested rollback procedures.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize without baseline metrics or representative evaluation data.
Do not parallelize tasks that have unresolved dependencies or shared-state conflicts.
Do not reduce cost by accepting unmeasured quality degradation.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a runnable orchestration framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides methods and illustrative pseudocode that require implementation in your environment.

faq.question: Can it optimize a single agent prompt?
faq.answer: It is designed for multi-agent systems. Use focused prompt evaluation for a single agent.

faq.question: Which metrics should I collect first?
faq.answer: Collect latency, throughput, error rate, token usage, cost, and task-specific quality measures.

faq.question: How does it address model costs?
faq.answer: It recommends token tracking, caching, context controls, and model selection based on task complexity.

faq.question: Does it guarantee faster workflows?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on workload structure, dependencies, infrastructure, and measured implementation quality.

faq.question: Should recommendations be deployed directly to production?
faq.answer: No. Validate them with repeatable tests, gradual rollout, monitoring, and rollback criteria.
